title: Silver activity catalog v1
description: Human-named units of tool-using design work. An activity names a (capability, actions, artifact kinds) combination so a designer can bind a transport to it in plain language. Support is derived from provider and skill contracts, never declared here.

title.description: What a designer would call this. Shown wherever a transport is chosen or reported.

artifact_kinds.description: Narrows the activity to particular artifact kinds. This is what separates pushing a token source from pushing a flow when both are (design-file, write).

status.description: served: at least one shipped provider supports this activity. planned: a named gap with no shipped provider yet. Checked in both directions, so a new provider forces the status to be corrected.

phrases.description: What a designer would actually say. Matched by `silver tools --for "<phrase>"`; required because id/capability substring matching produces mass ambiguity across a namespaced vocabulary this size.

binding.description: bindable (default): a designer can choose and re-bind a transport for this activity. internal: no other provider can meaningfully serve this (typically because its capability is PACKAGE_ONLY, or no alternative is credible even in principle) — `silver tools --bind` refuses to bind these.

fallback.description: The native answer used when no provider matches this activity's capability. This is a separate resolution path, not a ranked-last provider: silver-portable answers it without needing to hold the activity's capability at all. Guarantees every activity has a Silver-native answer, however degraded.

mode.description: native: silver-portable performs the activity itself, fully. input-required: silver-portable can proceed only if given the missing input (an export, a URL, credentials). representational: silver-portable can describe or spec the thing but not produce the actual external artifact.

note.description: The plain-language assumption or instruction that goes with this fallback, e.g. "Analyze exported data if supplied; never invent live analytics results."
